prompt: John is a recent college graduate with very little experience in operating a business, but he wants to own a food-marketing business that has a well-known trade name. If he has sufficient capital to invest, what type of business ownership should he consider?
explanation: Business-format franchise. A business-format franchise is a franchise arrangement in which the franchisee must operate under the trade name of the parent company, which provides continuous assistance in setting up and operating the business. It is a popular type of franchise arrangement that is usually available to most anyone who has the capital to invest. A general partnership is an agreement in which all partners are liable for a business's losses. A sole proprietorship is a business owned by one person. A limited liability company is a form of business ownership in which members of a corporation experience limited liability.

prompt: Which of the following is a rule of good listening:
choices: Be thinking about what you will say next.
Stand as close as possible to the speaker.
explanation: Listen with empathy. Empathy is the ability to put oneself in another person's place. Listening with empathy helps the listener to understand the speaker's point of view. You should stand a reasonable distance from the speaker. Standing too close may be interpreted as aggressiveness. If you are thinking about what you will say next, you may not hear everything that the speaker says. Background noise exists in all environments and cannot be eliminated.

prompt: In the following situation at the YumYum Gourmet Food Company, what did Samantha fail to do: "Hello. This is Samantha. How may I help you? I'll need your name, address, and account number. That was one #89306 and two #63085. Thank you for calling in your order."
choices: Repeat the order to the customer
explanation: Identify the company. Techniques for handling incoming calls correctly include identifying the company as well as yourself, repeating the order to the customer to make sure it is correct, and closing the conversation courteously. Samantha did all of these except identify the company.

prompt: Employees of large supermarkets should know the locations of various departments so they can
explanation: Give directions to customers. Many modern supermarkets are extremely large and contain a variety of departments. Customers may have trouble remembering where each department is located and need directions. Supermarket employees should be familiar with the various locations and what is available in each department in order to give directions to customers. Employees of large supermarkets do not need to know the locations of various departments in order to help coworkers stock shelves, answer telephone inquiries, or assist vendors with problems.

prompt: A supermarket customer wants to purchase an advertised product, but the product is not in stock. This is an example of a problem in the area of distribution known as
explanation: Inventory control. Controlling inventory involves keeping track of how much stock is on hand, how much has been sold, and how much is on order. A benefit of inventory control is the prevention of stockouts; a situation in which there is no stock of an inventory item on hand. Leasing is contracting to use property that belongs to someone else for a specific period of time for a specific amount of rent. Warehousing involves placing goods in safe locations until they are needed or are ready to be sold. Stock handling includes the loading, unloading, and handling of goods.

prompt: Wingo's Gourmet Cookies sells the bakery items it produces through its own catalog, which is a form of ___________ distribution.
explanation: Direct. Direct distribution is a channel of distribution in which goods and services move directly from the producer to the consumer or industrial user. Indirect distribution is where goods and services move from the producer to the channel members and then to consumers or industrial users. Industrial and middleman are not terms that are used to describe businesses that sell products directly to consumer or end users.

prompt: A snack-food manufacturer who wants a grocery store to carry a new product might pay the grocery store a slotting allowance to cover the cost of
explanation: Cents-off coupons. A slotting allowance is a cash premium that food manufacturers pay to supermarkets to cover the costs involved in carrying a new food item. The money is intended to pay for such expenses as the cost involved in offering cents-off coupons to encourage customers to try the new product. A slotting allowance also pays for shelf space, store advertising, and penalties if the product doesn't sell. Manufacturers often pay licensing fees to sports teams or famous people in order to use their names or logos on products. Sales incentives are bonuses or awards given to employees who meet or exceed their sales quotas. Mail-in rebates are a sales promotion activity that involves the manufacturer returning part of the price a customer pays for a good or service.

prompt: Which of the following is a form used by some specialty food stores to record errors found in incoming shipments of merchandise:
explanation: Discrepancy report. This is a form used to record shortages, damage, or any other irregularities found in a food shipment. A packing list is a list of the contents of the shipment provided by the seller. A dummy invoice is a checker's list of what the shipment contains. The receiving record is the record of all goods received by a specialty food store.

prompt: A reason that customers return merchandise that can be corrected by the business is
explanation: Poor selling practices. The business can prevent some merchandise returns by making sure that salespeople are well trained and knowledgeable about the products they sell. Salespeople should identify customer needs and make every effort to help the customer avoid a hasty decision or a mistake, but the business cannot prevent these things from happening. It also is not responsible for defective materials used in making a product.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a supermarket bakery filling orders for customers:
explanation: Processing telephone requests. Supermarket bakeries often accept telephone requests from customers. For example, a customer might call and ask the bakery to prepare a pastry tray for the customer to pick up later that day. When a supermarket bakery processes these requests, it is filling orders for customers. Sending monthly statements is the way that some retailers (e.g., department stores) bill their credit customers. Depending on the type of product that a supermarket customer wants, a store employee might check the delivery schedules to set a time to deliver the order. When a customer places an order, some retailers might review inventory to make sure the specified item is in stock before fulfilling the order.

prompt: One reason why it is important for grocery stores to maintain adequate inventory levels is to avoid __________ needed goods.
explanation: Running out of. Grocery stores need to maintain adequate inventory levels in order to operate. Grocery stores may not be able to function at their best if they run out of the goods they resell to customers. If grocery stores run out of these items, customers will not be satisfied and the grocery store will lose sales. Sometimes, grocery stores stockpile certain inventory items if they think a shortage will occur or if prices will increase drastically. Grocery stores do not maintain adequate inventory levels in order to avoid paying taxes or depreciating the goods.

prompt: Moving a food product to market and making it available and accessible to customers are important activities that influence the rest of the
explanation: Marketing mix. Although distribution decisions do not necessarily precede other marketing decisions, they must be acknowledged as an important influence on the marketing mix of a food product. Food products must be available and accessible in order for customers to be able to buy. Product mix, promotional plans, and merchandise plans are also considered in the marketing mix.

prompt: What type of channel conflict might occur if the manufacturer of a specific brand begins to allow retailers other than the authorized retailers to sell the brand-name products?
explanation: Vertical. Vertical conflict occurs among different levels of the same channel of distribution, such as between a manufacturer and its authorized retailers. If a manufacturer begins to allow retailers other than those currently authorized to sell the brand-name products, the retailers may become upset because others now have the same products. Expanding the number of outlets for the products may be good for the manufacturer but detrimental to the retailers because they will have more competition. Horizontal conflict occurs among businesses at the same channel level, such as between the authorized businesses in the same city. Contractual and industrial are not types of channel conflict.

prompt: A supermarket might place baked goods near the delicatessen because many items in the bakery and delicatessen departments are
explanation: Complementary. Supermarkets categorize items and place them in certain areas of a store in order to maximize sales. One way to categorize items is to consider complementary items, or goods that are used together. To make a sandwich, customers need bread, rolls, or buns as well as lunchmeat. Therefore, supermarkets can maximize sales by placing these types of items in the same area of the store. Supermarkets do not place baked goods near the delicatessen because items are discounted or competitive. Food is tangible rather than intangible.

prompt: What can a ice-cream producer do to overcome a problem with limited human resources?
explanation: Offer training and retraining. Human resources are the people who work to produce goods (e.g., ice cream) and services. Training and retraining helps workers to develop new skills and to do a better job. When resources are limited, producers are more likely to increase the use of automation and increase benefits. An increase in the use of natural resources, items that are found in nature, would not influence the supply of human resources.

prompt: What might cease if food producers decide that their incomes are inadequate to continue making food items?
explanation: Consumption. Consumption is the process or activity of using goods and services. If producers decide that their incomes are not adequate, they may choose not to make products. If goods and services are not available, consumption would cease. Competition is rivalry between two or more businesses to attract customer dollars. Competition is good for the economy because it helps strong businesses to thrive and prosper and make more goods and services available for consumption. Compensation is wages, salary, incentives, and benefits offered to employees. Communication is an exchange of information in which the words and gestures are understood in the same way by both the speaker and the listener.

prompt: The headquarters for Ryder's supermarket chain is located in a large city, is one of the largest employers in the area, and has a strong commitment to giving money and support to local schools. In this situation, the Ryder's supermarket chain is being socially responsible to
explanation: The community. By giving money to the schools, Ryder's supermarket chain is directly benefiting the students and teachers, and indirectly benefiting the students' parents, potential employers, and other community members. Although the students and community members may also be consumers of Ryder's products, they are not being benefited through the use of those products. Ryder's employees, although they may be community members, are not being benefited through their work. The company is not being socially responsible to itself, although it may benefit from the good publicity its actions generate.

prompt: A disadvantage of government ownership of business in a communist command economy is
explanation: Lack of competition. Government ownership eliminates competition, which may result in higher prices, smaller selections, and lower product quality. Government ownership usually includes detailed central planning. Resources may be used less efficiently because businesses are not free to increase their productivity by finding less costly and time-consuming methods of production.

prompt: Which of the following is a direct result of increased productivity:
explanation: Higher standard of living. The standard of living is the quality of life, or the general conditions in which people live. A high standard of living is a direct result of high productivity. Workers increase their productivity in order to earn higher wages with which to buy the things that they want, and they tend to enjoy a higher standard of living as a result of their productivity. Increased productivity does not result in a rise in consumer prices, greater business liability, or a higher failure rate of businesses.

prompt: A group of workers who have joined together for a common purpose is called a(n)
explanation: Labor union. A labor union is made up of workers who want to improve the terms and conditions under which they work. A union shop and an agency shop are types of union security agreements. A federation is made up of many national unions.

prompt: What effect is the continued growth of international trade having on the food marketing industry?
explanation: Increasing competition. The food marketing industry continues to become more global in nature as international corporations buy supermarket chains, food producers, and wholesalers throughout the world. The result is increased competition. Local stores face stiff competition from international giants that have the buying power to offer an enormous range of products at low prices. These giants also compete with each other for worldwide markets. The growth of international trade in food marketing provides a broader range of goods to consumers at lower prices. The large food corporations are able to quickly distribute products to all parts of the world.

prompt: Determine whether the following statement is true or false: Humor is a desirable personality trait for a businessperson.
choices: False, humor makes being an effective leader more difficult.
False, humor detracts from your professional image.
True, humor can make you appear more dependable.
True, humor can make people around you more comfortable.
explanation: True, humor can make people around you more comfortable. It also helps individuals to handle stress and maintain self-control, especially during trying situations. Humor is not an indication of dependability. Humor may make you a better leader by improving your attitude and your ability to show patience and tolerance.

prompt: Giving a wrong or false impression about something or someone is known as
explanation: Misrepresentation. Personal needs, desires, motivation, and lack of knowledge/understanding influence the accuracy with which facts are interpreted and communicated. To avoid misrepresentations, a person needs to collect all of the facts, interpret them accurately, and communicate them honestly. Empathy is the ability to put oneself in another's situation. An employee who is a self-starter has initiative. Enthusiasm is demonstrating a high degree of interest or approval.

prompt: One of the benefits to you of receiving feedback on the job is that it
choices: helps you to understand the supervisor.
lets you know how you are doing.
makes you feel like a valued employee.
explanation: Lets you know how you are doing. Feedback on the job lets you know whether you are exceeding, meeting, or falling short of the business's expectations. It lets you know whether you should continue as you are or change. Only positive feedback would raise your self-esteem or make you feel valued. Feedback is not intended to help you understand your supervisor but to understand yourself.

prompt: Graduation from an educational institution would be an example of a(n) __________ change.
explanation: Personal. Personal changes are those that concern our bodies, minds, lifestyles, etc. These changes are frequent and obvious in our personal lives. Where we live, what we do, who our friends are, etc., are always subject to change and may be influenced by economic, governmental, or technological changes. Economic changes are fluctuations in the economy. Governmental changes are new or revised laws, regulations, policies, public leadership, etc. Technological changes are developments, breakthroughs, and other changes in the fields of science, engineering, etc.

prompt: As supermarket employees go about their daily activities, their actions should be driven by whether the actions will
explanation: Result in customer satisfaction. Making customers feel important is a goal of demonstrating a customer-service mindset. Supermarket customers should feel welcome and that their satisfaction is important to everyone concerned. By focusing on the customers' needs, employees can increase sales and benefit the supermarket. The customer-service mindset should be practiced by all supermarket employees regardless of whether employees have direct contact with customers.

prompt: Food-marketing executives who respect the unique customs and habits of their foreign customers are exhibiting
explanation: Cultural sensitivity. Culture is the customs, habits, and traditions of a particular group of people. The way that different people interact with each other is an expression of their culture. Food-marketing executives need to be sensitive to the fact that their foreign customers may have unique customs such as bowing when they greet each other rather than shaking hands. They should accept these customs and try to make their foreign customers feel comfortable. Food-marketing executives who behave in this manner are showing respect for other customs and habits and are exhibiting cultural sensitivity. Communication skills are abilities to express yourself clearly and simply. Stereotypical behavior involves acting in a manner that conforms to a set image. Language differences occur when people speak different languages.

prompt: In order for communication to take place, there must be both
explanation: Senders and receivers. Any communication process must have a sender—one who dispatches information—and a receiver—one who accepts information. Distortions and distractions are barriers to good communication. Verbal and nonverbal are types of communication. Reading and writing are methods of communication.

prompt: Grocery stores develop policies to help employees deal with customers the same way in similar situations so that the employees will
explanation: Treat customers fairly. Management establishes policies that help grocery store employees to deal with customers in the same way for the same situation in order to be fair. Customers who are not treated fairly may take their business elsewhere. Grocery stores do not develop policies to treat customers differently, to offer special privileges, or to give personal favors.

prompt: Which of the following would be classified as a service complaint:
explanation: Late delivery. The quality of service provided customers can result in complaints. For example, customers will complain when deliveries are late. A defective item or incorrect size are product complaints. Empathetic behavior should result in customer satisfaction rather than in customer complaints.

prompt: What type of financial records do supermarkets need to maintain in order to keep track of their transactions?
explanation: Accounts receivable. Accounts receivable are the monies owed to a supermarket by its customers. Supermarkets maintain financial records that include an exact listing of each transaction that occurs in the supermarket. The records include expenses, money received, and any money owed, which is referred to as accounts receivable. Supermarkets need to know how much money will be coming in over a period of time in order to keep track of current financial status. Tax identification, payroll information, and operating procedures are not types of financial records that supermarkets need to maintain in order to keep track of their transactions.

prompt: A business files and pays state sales tax before the due date each month in order to take the .075% discount on the amount of tax due. The business collected 5% sales tax on sales of $25,000 in June. How much did the business save by paying the sales tax on time?
explanation: $93.75. The business sold $25,000 in taxable goods and collected the 5% state sales tax. Multiply $25,000 by 5% or .05 to determine that the business collected $1,250 in sales tax ($25,000 x 5% or .05 = $1,250). Multiply $1,250 by .075 to determine the discount of $93.75 ($1,250 x .075 = $93.75).

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement about a specialty food store's endorsements of checks for deposit:
choices: Federal regulations determine location of the endorsement.
"For deposit only" is part of a blank endorsement.
State regulations determine the type of endorsement used.
Only one check in a deposit needs to be endorsed.
explanation: Federal regulations determine location of the endorsement. One area on the trailing edge, or reverse of the left side, of the check is allocated for the endorsement. This standard procedure enables the bank to process the checks quickly. There are no state regulations on the type of endorsement to be used. "For deposit only" is a restricted endorsement used to ensure that checks will be deposited and not cashed illegally. All checks in a deposit need to be endorsed or stamped.

prompt: What type of data is the most expensive to gather for a supermarket chain?
explanation: Primary. Primary data are facts collected for use in one particular situation. They are gathered in a systematic manner to solve a problem, explore an opportunity, or for any other purpose useful to the supermarket. Some ways in which primary data are gathered include questioning employees, customers, or competitors; or hiring a marketing-research company to obtain the primary data. All of these activities can be expensive. Secondary data are less expensive to gather because they have already been collected for some other purpose. Internal data are facts collected within the supermarket chain through normal record-keeping procedures. External data are facts collected outside the supermarket chain.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a grocer obtaining marketing information about consumers in a way that might be considered unethical:
choices: Offering a free product in exchange for personal data
Sending questionnaires to a specific audience
explanation: Offering a free product in exchange for personal data. Certain ways of obtaining marketing information may be considered unethical even though they are legal. An example is offering free products in exchange for personal data. Consumers may be persuaded to provide information that they normally would not provide simply because the offer is so tempting, or they need the product being offered. Furthermore, consumers have no guarantee that the grocer will keep the personal data confidential. In some cases, the grocers try to obtain this information in order to sell it to others. Most grocers follow ethical procedures when obtaining marketing information about consumers. These procedures might include conducting a random survey, sending questionnaires to a specific audience, and developing an experiment.

prompt: Why do many food marketers use computer technology to manage marketing information?
choices: To merge a variety of data into one database
To send direct-mail pieces to customers
To develop software that fits a specific need
explanation: To merge a variety of data into one database. Food marketers often obtain information about customers from a variety of sources such as questionnaires, warranty cards, or sweepstakes entries. All of this information is valuable if the food marketers are able to merge it into a database that is easily accessible. A food marketer's customer database might include information about name, address, types of recent purchases, dollar amounts spent, general interests, income, brand preferences, etc. Food marketers use the merged database to target specific customers or identify trends in order to remain competitive. Food marketers might purchase software in order to prepare questionnaires or direct-mail pieces that will be sent to customers, but not to manage marketing information.

prompt: Food distributors use the information from sales representatives to make decisions. One type of report that details a sales representative's planned sales calls and routes for an upcoming week or month is a(n) __________ report.
explanation: Activity. An activity report describes a sales representative's intended sales calls and routes and is submitted to management a week or month in advance. Food distributors often use the information in these reports to make marketing decisions. A call report is a write-up of completed sales activities. Territory and quota reports do not include planned activities of individual sales representatives.

prompt: A marketing-research project that gathers sufficient information to help a specialty food store in its decision making would be described as
explanation: Thorough. An important characteristic of effective marketing research is that it should be thorough. Incomplete or insufficient research won't give the specialty food store enough information to enable it to make good decisions. The way in which the research is carried out would determine whether or not it was efficient. Predictive research is marketing research used to help the specialty food store forecast future business developments. Some aspects of marketing research are tedious, tiresome, monotonous, or boring, but these aspects are not necessarily related to the amount of information gathered.

prompt: An important reason why a grocery store develops marketing strategies is to give the store
explanation: Direction. Marketing strategies are plans of action that give direction to a grocery store's goals and objectives. Having marketing strategies helps the grocery store to determine where it will place its efforts or resources. Without the direction provided by marketing strategies, a grocery store would not have organization and focus when carrying out its marketing activities. This lack of direction would be confusing to customers and to the store's employees. Objectives are goals to be reached. A grocery store establishes its goals and objectives before developing marketing strategies. Credibility is believability. Identity is the name or perception of the grocery store.

prompt: Dividing a total market into smaller, more specific groups is known as
explanation: Market segmentation. Rather than trying to direct marketing activities at the whole market, marketers plan their activities for specific, well-defined groups of consumers. They tailor their product, price, place, and promotion activities to the segments with which they wish to work. Marketing is the process of planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion, and distribution of ideas, goods, and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organizational objectives. With mass marketing, sellers design products that will appeal to most buyers and direct marketing activities to the whole market. Target marketing is the identification and selection of markets for a business or for a product.

prompt: Which of the following is an important part of a supermarket's marketing plan:
explanation: Promotional activities. A marketing plan is a set of procedures or strategies for attracting the target customer to a supermarket. An important part of a marketing plan is the promotional activities that a supermarket will use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of its products. Supermarkets need to identify these activities which may include advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, and publicity. Human resources are the people who work to produce goods or services. Purchasing policies are guidelines that direct purchasing decisions. An operating system involves the activities needed to run the supermarket on a day-to-day basis.

prompt: What are bakeries examining when they conduct a situational analysis during the marketing-planning process?
explanation: Environmental factors. The purpose of a situational analysis is to examine and interpret the environmental factors that affect the bakery. The environmental factors may be internal, such as a bakery's distribution system or pricing strategy, as well as external, such as the state of the economy or the number of competitors. Bakeries examine both types of environmental factors in order to adapt to change and make effective marketing decisions. For example, if the economy is slowing down, a bakery might decide to adjust its prices to remain competitive. Physical characteristics are personal traits such as age, height, weight, etc. Personal aptitudes are a person's natural talents. Geographical changes involve changes in natural features or climate.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an external change that could affect a supermarket's sales forecast:
choices: The town's population increases when a new manufacturing plant opens in the community.
A new executive has been hired to develop the supermarket's presence in a neighboring state.
The supermarket plans to modify its approach to advertising to customers.
The company plans to raise prices on some of its products.
explanation: The population of a town increases when a new manufacturing plant opens in the community. External changes occur outside the supermarket, and the supermarket has no control over these changes. Examples of external changes that may affect sales forecasts are population changes, economic changes, competitive changes, and market changes. Internal changes, on the other hand, are circumstances that occur within the supermarket over which the supermarket has some degree of control. Such factors would include changes in personnel, promotion, and pricing.

prompt: A grocer adds an area for the local college's licensed sportswear and novelty items in the store. This is an example of
explanation: Scrambled merchandising. Scrambled merchandising is a strategy for increasing sales by adding product lines that are dissimilar. Product positioning is the consumer's image of a product as compared to that of competitive products. Public relations is a promotional activity designed to establish good relations between a business and the public. Profit maximization is a profit-oriented pricing objective intended to give the firm the most possible profit.

prompt: By enabling consumers to obtain goods and services at the right time and in the right place, food marketers are trying to add __________ to goods and services.
explanation: Utility. Usefulness, or utility, is added to goods and services when they are made available to consumers. Food marketers do not try to increase costs since that would reduce their profits. Production capacity refers to the amount of goods and services a company can produce. Buying power is the consumer's ability to purchase.

prompt: In order to operate an optical scanner properly, the food marketing cashier should use it on products labeled with which of the following:
explanation: UPC code. Universal product codes are a series of bars and numbers that contain product information that is read by an optical scanner. The cashier passes the product over the optical scanner. POS is a point-of-sale computer system. UVM is universal vendor marking, which is a type of code read by a hand-held electronic wand. COD is cash on delivery means that a shipment must be paid for at the time of delivery.

prompt: Information about how well an item sold during a recent advertising campaign usually is kept in a grocery store's __________ records.
explanation: Promotional. Promotional records contain information about the various types of communications that grocery stores use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of their products. Advertising is a promotional message; therefore, information about an advertised item, how well it sold, a description of the ad, and other related data would be maintained in a grocery store's promotional records. Financial records contain information related to the amount of money going into and out of a business. Administrative records help to ensure the smooth operation of a business. Professional is not a type of business record.

prompt: What type of software program do food marketers use to create text documents?
explanation: Word processing. Most word-processing software programs are designed to be used to create text documents, although some have limited graphic capabilities. Food marketers use word-processing software programs to write letters, memos, reports, business plans, and sales contracts. There are many different word-processing software programs available that enable food marketers to create, edit, and store important text documents. Presentation software programs are used to develop visual presentations. Web-page editors are software applications that food marketers use to create web pages. Communications software programs allow computers to communicate with other computers.

prompt: A grocery store wants to purchase computer software that would maintain and analyze customer information in order to better serve customer needs and increase sales. What type of software should the business buy?
explanation: Database. A database program allows the organized collection of information with pieces of information related to one another. This information can be used to maintain, analyze, and combine customer information. Spreadsheets, word-processing software, and computer-aided design do not perform the functions required by the grocery store.

prompt: Stock turnover information indicating that some merchandise is moving slowly helps the grocery stores decide whether to
explanation: Purchase more goods. The stock turnover rate provides grocery stores with information about how quickly merchandise is selling. If the information indicates that some merchandise is moving slowly, grocery stores would decide not to purchase more of it. The stock turnover information helps grocery stores decide when the time is right to purchase goods or to reduce prices in order to sell slow-moving items. Stock turnover information does not help grocery stores decide when to remodel the facilities or expand the sales force.

prompt: In the food marketing industry, which of the following is often one of the first steps in the buying process:
explanation: Identifying customer needs. The food marketer needs to know its customers' needs before it takes any further steps. After determining needs, the buyer must identify and select sources of supply, must place the order, and obtain customer feedback in order to evaluate the purchases.

prompt: What type of form do many supermarkets require employees to complete when they are injured on the job?
explanation: Accident report. An accident report is a form completed by employees and/or supervisors to report specific details of workplace accidents. Many supermarkets require employees to complete an accident report form immediately or soon after an accident. Most forms require the employee to write a detailed account of the accident and its outcome. Supermarkets do not require employees to complete insurance application, medical records, or legal documents when they are injured on the job.

prompt: A new grocery store cashier handled customer's purchases without noticing that the customer's signature did not match the imprint from the charge card. Which of the following kinds of security precautions might have prevented this loss to the store:
explanation: Fraud prevention. Fraud is deceiving or cheating an individual or a grocery store out of money or property. Grocery stores usually instruct their employees to check the status of credit cards, the card's expiration date, and the signature on the back of the card. Employees should make sure that the signature on the charge receipt matches the signature on the back of the credit card. Pilferage is theft of small sums of money or inexpensive items. Robbery is theft that involves the use of force, violence, or fear. Burglary is any illegal entry into a building to commit a theft.

prompt: Soft-drink manufacturers that use the mass production process make products that are
explanation: Standardized. The mass production process only works efficiently when the products being produced are standardized or very similar. Mass production relies on using interchangeable parts and performing the same functions repeatedly. The process produces large quantities of similar items. Diversified, unique, and variable are terms describing products that are not standardized and cannot be made by the mass production process.

prompt: Determine whether the following statement is true or false: Most people have the same kind of work style.
choices: True, most people do their best work in the morning.
False, work style has been divided into categories.
False, each individual has a work style of his/her own.
True, most people approach tasks in the same way.
explanation: False, each individual has a work style of his/her own. Most people have a work style that suits them, which they have developed over time. No two people have the same approach. Work style has not been divided into specific categories, although individuals may be categorized as morning or afternoon people according to the time of day at which they are at their best.

prompt: Which of the following often is a reason why some specialty food stores fail:
explanation: Uncontrolled expenses. Uncontrolled expenses usually result in reduced profit, which often lead to business failure, if it is not corrected in time. Specialty food stores should carefully control their expenses in order to make sure they are not spending more than they can afford to spend based on their income. A dedicated work force, limited competition, and strong management usually are factors that contribute to a specialty grocery store's success.

prompt: Your goal is to become a regional manager for a national supermarket chain within five years after your hiring. This goal would be classified as a __________ goal.
explanation: Long-term, career. The goal is long term because it will take more than a year to accomplish, and it is a career goal because it involves a job. Educational goals involve learning activities, financial goals involve money, and social goals involve entertainment and interpersonal relationships.

prompt: Which of the following is a source of information about careers that is available at state and federal government agencies:
explanation: Civil service office. Information about careers with government agencies is available at civil service offices, which are responsible for hiring people for many of the positions in government. Civil service offices maintain lists of current jobs available, provide information about the job requirements, and administer tests to applicants. For example, a state civil service office would have information about all jobs currently available within all state agencies. National labor unions, local trade associations, and chambers of commerce do not have information about careers in government.

prompt: One of the reasons why it is important for food marketers to continue their education throughout their careers is to be prepared for
explanation: Jobs of the future. Food marketers will experience many changes in technology throughout their careers. In order to be prepared for the jobs that new technology will create, employees need to continue their education. Technology will eliminate some jobs in the future and change the way some jobs are performed. Food marketers will need to keep up with the new developments by continuing their education and learning new skills. Those food marketers who do not continue their education might find themselves without jobs because they have not adapted to a new work environment. Food marketers do not continue their education in order to be prepared for life after retirement, changes in lifestyle, or adjustments in pay. However, continuing their education often helps food marketers to improve their lifestyle by increasing their pay.

prompt: One of the reasons why networking is so effective is because the contacts often
choices: work at the supermarket chain that is hiring.
are interested in the same supermarket position.
have information about food marketers' job skills.
know how to communicate with food marketing employees.
explanation: Work at the supermarket chain that is hiring. Many of the people in a network are professionals that the individual knows because of business or work-related activities. The advantage of including these people in a network is that they often work at the supermarket that is hiring and can pass on information to others in the network. If the contacts are interested in the same position, they might not be willing to network and share information. The contacts may have information about food marketers' job skills and know how to communicate with food marketing employees, but those are not reasons why networking is so effective.

prompt: Which one of the following occupations in the food marketing industry often requires employees to have college degrees, pass certain tests, and be licensed:
explanation: Inspector. There are many types of inspectors in the food marketing industry, and their main function is to guarantee the safety of the food supply. These inspectors routinely check on businesses that produce, process, package, store, and transport food products. As a result, they need a good understanding of a variety of subjects such as agriculture, biology, health, etc. Most obtain college degrees in specific areas, pass certain tests, and are licensed. The role of inspectors will continue to increase as governments develop additional regulations to make sure that food is free from contamination and safe for consumption. Managers, bakers, and meat cutters do not need to have college degrees, pass certain tests, or be licensed. However, meat cutters are often required to be certified.

prompt: What do food marketers that are involved in non-store retailing often use to increase sales?
explanation: Catalogs. Food marketers that are involved in non-store retailing often develop catalogs and mail them to potential customers in order to increase sales. The catalogs list all of the food products as well as ordering information. Customers may mail in an order form or access a company's web site to place an online order. The catalogs create an incentive to buy because they show the products in an attractive manner and include an appealing description. The ease of ordering is another incentive to buy. Because of the nature of non-store retailing, it is not possible to use displays, kiosks, or demonstrations to increase sales.

prompt: King's Food Mart spends less on advertising than Cameron's Supermarket. Both stores sell the same products, but Cameron's Supermarket charges higher prices than King Food Mart. Which of the following factors has affected the prices of the store:
explanation: Promotion. Cameron's Supermarket is spending more on its advertising and is passing the costs on to the customer through higher prices. Place involves getting products in the right place at the right time. Product decisions involve deciding what goods, services, or ideas to produce or to sell in order to satisfy customers' needs and wants. Supply is the quantity of a good or service that sellers are able and willing to offer for sale at a specified price in a given time period.

prompt: In the food marketing industry, which of the following pricing tactics might be considered questionable or unethical:
choices: Matching the prices of a competitor
Marking up prices to earn a profit
explanation: Developing a complex pricing structure. Some food marketers develop complex pricing structures that are very difficult for their customers to understand. Customers buying from such businesses are seldom able to figure out how to get a lower price and end up spending more than they should. Although this practice is not illegal, it is considered unethical because customers don't have a fair chance to obtain the best price. Providing a reference price is ethical because it gives customers a comparison price. It is ethical for food marketers to match the prices of competitors as long as they don't meet in advance and agree to set the prices. The purpose of business is to earn a profit, which involves marking up prices.

prompt: Price discrimination is legal in all of the following situations except when
choices: price differs to meet competitors’ prices.
explanation: Prices inhibit competition. The Robinson-Patman Act (1936) restricts price discrimination practices. It is illegal for a manufacturer to charge different prices to different businesses for the same products if it impairs competition. Price discrimination is legal in the other situations.

prompt: During the growth stage of the product life cycle, a snack-food company's marketing efforts usually involve advertising
choices: the unique benefits of the product.
the discounts that are being offered.
that competitors' products are not as popular.
that customers are satisfied with the product.
explanation: That customers are satisfied with the product. Sales and profits increase during the growth stage of the product life cycle. Many customers are aware of the product and buy the product. To maintain sales, a snack-food company usually starts to focus on advertising that customers are satisfied with the product. It is more effective to promote customer satisfaction than to promote the product's benefits because most people are aware of the benefits. People are more likely to continue buying during the growth stage if they think that other people are satisfied with the product. Snack-food companies usually advertise the unique benefits of the product during the introduction stage. Snack-food companies often advertise that competitors' products are not as popular during the maturity stage. A snack-food company is likely to advertise discounts during the decline stage.

prompt: One way that advances in technology are impacting the product/service management function is by making it possible for food marketers to
explanation: Improve existing products. As a result of advances in technology, new processes and operating techniques have been developed. These processes and techniques have made it possible for food marketers to improve existing products. This impacts the product/service management function because it enables food marketers to extend the life of existing products and keep them on the market. Food marketers have found that it is usually less expensive to update existing products than to develop entirely new products. Advances in technology are allowing food marketers to do this. Advances in technology often help to reduce human errors but cannot completely eliminate them. Advances in technology often make production systems more complex because they rely on complicated computer systems. Food marketers are not able to control customer preferences.

prompt: Why do many food-processing companies package their food products in tamper-resistant containers?
explanation: To protect customers. Many food processing companies have developed ethical standards to follow in an effort to protect their products and ensure the safety of their customers. One method being used to protect consumers is tamper-resistant containers. Customers are able to easily determine if this type of packaging has been tampered with which warns them not to buy the product. Food-processing companies do not use tamper-resistant packaging in order to save the environment, recycle plastic, or promote social issues. The purpose of the tamper-resistant packaging is to protect consumers and the food supply.

prompt: The Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act is a federal statute intended to assure consumers that the products they buy will be safe, which means that the products are
explanation: Pure and meet certain standards. The Food and Drug Administration enforces the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to ensure that food products are unadulterated, correctly labeled, meet certain quality standards, and are safe. People, rather than products, may be free from fear and danger. Safe does not mean that products are covered by a written warranty or are manufactured by professionals.

prompt: What might decrease if a snack-food company adds an inappropriate item to the product mix?
explanation: Profits. A snack-food company might experience a decrease in profits if it adds an inappropriate item to the product mix. An inappropriate item might compete with the original goods, which would cause sales of the original goods to decline and sales for the new item to be less than expected. The snack-food company should make sure that their product mix is appropriate in order to increase sales and profits. Expenses are the monies that a business spends. Prices are the amounts of money paid for a good, service, or resource. Salaries are money payments for labor.

prompt: Which of the following categories of food has a high sales volume and usually is placed near the entrance of the grocery store:
explanation: Produce. Produce includes a wide variety of fresh fruits and vegetables and is one of the main categories of food in a grocery store. Produce has a high sales volume, which is one of the reasons why it is placed near the store's entrance. Attractively displayed fresh produce appeals to customers and encourages them to buy. As a result, the produce department is often one of the largest areas of the store. The dry foods category includes cereal, which usually is located in the middle of the store. Seafood and frozen items generally do not have the high sales volume that produce has, and these items often are located in the back of the store or in the last aisle, respectively.

prompt: A food company that says it tries harder because its product is not number one, is using product positioning to
explanation: Compete. Food companies often position their products to compete successfully with other, similar products. Saying that they try harder because their products are not number one is a way of positioning products to compete. The goal is to make the product stand out and draw attention to the fact that, although the product is the same as competitors' products, the food company will try harder to satisfy customers. A food company that says it tries harder is not using product positioning to motivate, organize, or upgrade.

prompt: Which of the following would be characteristic of a good brand name in the food-marketing industry:
explanation: Easily pronounced. A good brand name should also be short, easy to spell, distinctive, adaptable, easily recognized, timely, and versatile. Selling well-known brand names is a good way to get repeat business.

prompt: Supermarkets calculate the open-to-buy amount by subtracting the dollar value of products on order from planned
explanation: Purchases. Planned purchases are the total dollar amount of products that a supermarket intends to order during a certain period of time. Open-to-buy is the amount of money left to spend during a specified period of time. The way to determine how much money is left to spend is to subtract the dollar amount of items on order from the total dollar amount that was budgeted for purchases. Planned sales is the amount the supermarket expects to sell during a specific period of time. Reductions include markdowns, discounts, and inventory shortages.

prompt: Determine whether the following is a true statement: It is important for a food marketer's promotional message to be factual.
choices: True, it should alter facts as necessary.
True, it must be based on facts.
False, it need not be based on facts.
False, it must only be memorable.
explanation: True, it must be based on facts. The way in which a promotional message is presented can be creative, but it must be based on fact. The facts should not be altered, since this may mislead the customer. The message should be memorable, but that is not its only characteristic.

prompt: What type of promotion would the Friendly Food Mart grocery store chain use to inform consumers about the company's commitment to social and environmental issues?
explanation: Institutional. Institutional promotion aims to create a certain image in the eyes of consumers. Institutional promotion does not attempt to sell a good or service, but tries to inform customers about the company, its ideas, its philosophy, and its position on important issues. Institutional promotion often is used to make consumers aware of a company's interest in social or environmental issues. Product promotion aims to persuade consumers to buy a good or service. Primary product promotion is intended to stimulate demand for an entire class of goods or services. Secondary product promotion is intended to stimulate demand for a particular brand of a product.

prompt: What is the combination of methods used by supermarkets to communicate with prospective consumers about their goods and services?
explanation: Promotional mix. There are a variety of ways in which supermarkets can transmit their message to the buying public. Most supermarkets choose a combination of methods geared to the particular market they wish to reach. The promotional mix includes the appropriate balance and selection of advertising media. Marketing mix is the combination of product, place, price, and promotion. Balanced promotion is not a method of communication.

prompt: A specialty grocery store that is found guilty of deceptive advertising is often required to place __________ advertising.
explanation: Corrective. Corrective advertising explains and amends information that was deceiving in a previous ad. If a specialty grocery store is found guilty of deceptive advertising, it is often required to develop corrective ads that will inform consumers about the misleading information and set the record straight. For example, if a specialty grocery store runs an ad that implies that a product will provide a certain benefit that it cannot provide, the specialty grocery store may be required to place a corrective ad that explains the inaccurate information. A comparative ad compares one product to another. Informative and affirmative are not specific types of advertising.

prompt: The primary cost factors that food marketers must consider when developing a direct advertising campaign include list acquisition, delivery, and
explanation: Production. The development or production of the direct advertising campaign might include the layout and printing costs of a brochure or catalog. Production needs are often outsourced to other companies and can be very expensive. Therefore, production costs are primary considerations when developing a direct advertising campaign. Inventory refers to the product that a company has available in stock. Research is the act of collecting information. Although research may cost a company money in terms of locating vendors (e.g., printers), this is not usually as costly as production. Therefore, research is not a primary cost. Follow-up is the determination of a customer's satisfaction with a good or service after a sales presentation, regardless of whether or not a sale was made.

prompt: What is the database that allows a supermarket chain to deal efficiently with very large amounts of data by linking the tables where data is stored?
explanation: Relational. A relational database-management system eliminates the need for storing the same information in several places by using codes to link tables together. A flat-file database is one that cannot be linked, such as a spreadsheet. A customized database is one that has been altered to meet a supermarket chain's exact needs. File Maker is a brand name.

prompt: Self-selection displays allow supermarket customers to __________ goods.
explanation: Handle. Self-selection displays provide supermarket customers with the opportunity to examine products, review labels and nutritional information and, in general, become familiar with the products. Supermarket customers do not purchase the products at the display location; they take the goods to the store's check-out area, where a cashier processes all sales transactions. These displays never allow the customer to mark down products.

prompt: How should a supermarket employee set up a stack display of cartons of soup cans so it is set up for maximum customer safety and convenience?
choices: Cut the top from each carton before stacking.
Stack the cans as high as possible.
Leave the cans in the closed cases.
Take the cans out of the cases before stacking.
explanation: Cut the top from each carton before stacking. This is often referred to as a cut-case display. The upper portion of the carton is cut away, leaving a tray to hold the cans. The tray keeps the cans in place, and it is easy for customers to read the labels on the cans. As the canned items are sold, the empty trays can be discarded. Stacking the cans, particularly stacking them as high as possible, could create a safety hazard as the stack of cans may topple. Leaving the cans in the closed cases makes them inaccessible to all customers except those who want to purchase an entire case.

prompt: To increase impulse sales of gum and candy, convenience stores might set up the product display
choices: on high shelves that are placed in the back of the store.
on low, open racks that are placed in front of the cash register.
in dump bins that are located near the beverage counter or rest rooms.
in cut cases that are below eye level and located near the dairy products.
explanation: On low, open racks that are placed in front of the cash register. Many factors must be considered when displaying food items, including location in the store, type of display unit, and physical and visual positioning (e.g., high or low eye level) of the products. By placing candy and gum near the cash register, all patrons are forced to see the goods. By placing the candy on open racks below eye level, customers can easily see and touch the items, including young children who often gravitate to these types of consumable items. When placing candy in dump bins or cut cases, customers must root through the box to find the items they want. As a result, some customers might feel that it takes too much effort to get their favorite sweet treats, and impulse sales are lost. Convenience stores do not always have beverage counters or indoor restrooms. Not all customers go to the back of the store or purchase dairy products, so the chances of increased impulse sales are greatly reduced in these locations.

prompt: What are the primary factors that supermarket managers consider when building food marketing displays?
explanation: Traffic and in-store placement. Many factors are considered when building food marketing displays, including product type, product arrangement, display size, in-store placement, and theme. For optimal exposure, managers must consider the traffic patterns within the store. For example, a display that is built near the store entrance will be seen by all shoppers, while an organic food display located in the rear corner of the store might have less traffic. Site location refers to the physical placement of the building and is not a primary factor when building food marketing display units. Not all food displays have audiovisual needs. Supplier preferences are often considered when building a food marketing display; however, stock-outs are issues most often addressed by purchasing personnel. Unless the display product is a stock-out item at the time of display construction, it is not considered a primary factor.

prompt: Situation analysis is the step in a supermarket's promotional planning process that involves determining the
choices: objectives of the firm's promotional program.
amount of money to spend on planned promotions.
current status of the firm in the marketplace.
elements to be included in the promotional mix.
explanation: Current status of the firm in the marketplace. A situation analysis reviews the target market, the supermarket's strengths and weaknesses, its promotional capabilities, its products, its market share, and any other factors that would affect promotional planning. Promotional objectives are the goals of the promotional program, and they are set according to the results of the situation analysis. Determining the amount of money in the promotional budget and the elements to be included in the promotional mix are later steps in the promotional planning process.

prompt: A supermarket chain that includes broadcast media in its promotional mix might coordinate commercial development activities with a(n)
explanation: Production house. Most supermarket chains do not have the in-house capabilities to develop professional television commercials. Supermarket chains often look to advertising agencies for creative ideas and to production houses for commercial production. It often takes many people to film a commercial, including filming crews, directors, and actors. A marketing-research firm might be used to find or compile information that a supermarket chain requests. A creative boutique is a firm that specializes in graphic design. An interactive agency is a business that provides services for web-based promotional activities.

prompt: As a supermarket equipment sales representative, Jason reads the instruction manuals that accompany the products he sells. This enables him to demonstrate his
explanation: Product knowledge. Salespeople can learn a great deal of specific product information about the items they sell by taking the time to read the manuals. Creativity is the ability to generate unique ideas. Ethical standards are unwritten rules of good conduct. Self-concept is the image you have of yourself.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement about selling policies:
choices: Most small, food-processing companies explain their selling policies in employee handbooks.
Selling policies are most useful for handling unusual situations that occur in supermarket chains.
Selling policies may be in writing or simply understood by grocery store employees.
The Sherman Act requires food marketers to put their selling policies in writing.
explanation: Selling policies may be in writing or simply understood by grocery store employees. Whether policies are written or orally stated usually depends on the nature of the organization, rather than on legislation. Food companies with a large sales force usually provide policy handbooks that are fully explained to all sales trainees. On the other hand, small food companies with few salespeople may operate without written policies. Selling policies establish uniform operating procedures for all salespeople in a food company to follow and are very useful in handling routine situations.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of using mapping software in the selling function:
explanation: Realigning sales territories. Mapping software is used in territory management and allows sales managers to create or realign territories and see an instant visual display of the effects. This software makes it possible for managers to input certain criteria, such as travel time and actual sales, and view a territory based on that information. Managers can experiment with various territories to find the ones that will be the most effective. Managers can also use mapping software to realign sales territories if the criteria change. Mapping software is not used to organize major accounts, track scheduled deliveries, or prepare sales brochures.

prompt: Which of the following is a statement that might violate certain selling regulations if it was posted on an online food equipment company's web site:
choices: This product comes with a warranty.
This product works in all situations.
explanation: This product works in all situations. This type of statement might violate certain selling regulations because it might be considered misrepresentation or over-exaggeration of the product's capabilities. Making such a bold statement is the same as saying that the product works all the time, in all situations, and without problems. If there are situations when this is not exactly true, the online food equipment company might be guilty of misrepresentation, which could lead to the food equipment company being sued. The best way to avoid this problem is to qualify the statement, such as "This product works in almost any situation." Stating that the product is great is the food equipment company's opinion, which is not misrepresentation. Stating that the product comes with a warranty is factual. Stating that the product might save money is also an opinion, which has been qualified by using the term "might."

prompt: A supermarket cashier scanning two separate items priced at 3 for $5.00 on an electronic cash register should
choices: expect the register to record the correct amounts.
explanation: Expect the register to record the correct amounts. Electronic cash registers with scanning devices are programmed to handle multiple-priced items whether they are presented together or separately. Only if this function fails to operate would the supermarket cashier need to calculate the correct amount and enter it manually. There is no 3 for $5.00 register key.

prompt: A catalog is a good source of __________ information for an online food marketer's employees.
explanation: Product. A great deal of product information is given in product catalogs, bulletins, and print advertisements. Employees who read these materials usually are able to obtain information that will help them sell products to customers. Manuals usually contain information about operating policies and procedures.

prompt: Ron is a clerk in a bakery and his brother is a car dealer. As salespeople, the brothers will
choices: spend a lot of time prospecting.
sell to the same type of customer.
explanation: Use the selling process differently. There is a difference in the use of the selling process depending on the nature of the product and the type of customer. Salespeople who sell inexpensive, frequently purchased items, such as bakery goods, do not need to prospect or qualify potential leads. Salespeople who sell large, expensive items, such as cars, usually need to do a lot of prospecting and spend time determining exactly what their customers want. Bakery customers usually know what they want, whereas customers buying cars may need a lot of assistance.

prompt: One of the fastest ways to determine customer needs is by
explanation: Asking open-ended questions. These questions encourage customers to talk because they cannot be answered with a simple yes or no. Consequently, open-ended questions encourage customers to discuss their needs and wants. Observation is not always accurate. Listening helps to determine customer needs only if the customer volunteers needed information. Assumptive questions check for understanding when the salesperson feels that s/he knows how the customer will respond.

prompt: Woody purchased the following: a gallon of milk for $2.59, one pound of apples at $1.98 per pound, a loaf of bread for $1.39, and a roast for $4.95. The store charges a 6.5% sales tax on all purchases. What was the amount of Woody's total purchase?
explanation: $11.62. Add together the cost of Woody's purchases, multiply by the rate of sales tax, and add the tax to the subtotal, rounding as necessary ($2.59 + $1.98 + $1.39 + $4.95 = $10.91; $10.91 x 6.5% or .065 = .709 or.71; $10.91 + .71 = $11.62).

prompt: In preparing for a sales presentation, a food distributor's new salesperson feels that s/he needs additional product information. An internal source of such information would be
explanation: Another salesperson. Experienced salespeople within the business can be an invaluable source of product information and are usually willing to share their experience with a new employee. A customer, the library, and the manufacturer are sources external to the business.

prompt: A supermarket cashier opened a cash register with a $50 change fund, and the register tape read $1,032.17 at the end of the shift. If the cashier has $24.63 in coins, $216.00 in paper money, $576.89 in checks, $12.65 in coupons, and deposited $250.00 in large bills during the shift, the cash count is
explanation: Short. The total of money, checks, coupons, and the early deposit was $1,080.17. After subtracting the opening change fund of $50.00, the checker has $1,030.17 in the drawer but should be accountable for $1,032.17, so the drawer is short $2.00. To be over, the cash total should be more than the register tape reading. The terms proved and even both mean that the cash total and the register reading are the same.

prompt: Delicatessen employees who take telephone orders for a supermarket should speak slowly and clearly in order to
explanation: Transmit information accurately. Delicatessen employees who take telephone orders must be sure that they speak slowly, enunciate clearly, and do not run their words together. These practices will encourage accurate transmission of information, which may determine whether the supermarket makes a sale. Customers should not be offended if the order taker does not speak slowly and clearly, but they may be frustrated in their efforts to obtain information. A supermarket delicatessen that receives telephone orders does not control the number of calls it receives. Good listening skills are required in order to receive the customer's order properly.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason that many supermarkets prefer to make even exchanges for nonfood items:
choices: The supermarket doesn't lose the sale.
The supermarket keeps the customer in the store.
explanation: The supermarket doesn't lose the sale. When handling nonfood merchandise, many supermarkets prefer even exchanges because no exchange of money takes place, a salesperson can handle the exchange, and a sale is still made. An even exchange does not necessarily keep the customer in the store. Supermarkets' preferences for even exchanges are not based on benefits to customers. Customers do not have the option of choosing higher or lower priced goods in an even exchange since it involves trading goods of equal value.

prompt: A common problem of first-level grocery-store supervisors is that they
choices: are unable to do long-range planning.
want to move up to mid-level.
are unfamiliar with the work they supervise.
explanation: Lack training in management techniques. Grocery stores often promote workers to supervisory jobs as a reward for good performance. These new supervisors often need training to help them assume supervisory responsibilities. First-level supervisors usually are familiar with the work because they have done it themselves. Long-range planning involves planning for the entire grocery store and is a responsibility of top management, not the first-level supervisor. Wanting to move up to mid-level management is not a problem but a legitimate career goal.
